Gastroenterology · published research

Perianal abscess

Summary of the Evidence

One human case report directly concerns a perianal abscess and describes incision and drainage followed by antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) and PBM. A separate rat study examined anal fistula, a related but distinct condition, so it provides adjacent evidence about fistula tissue rather than abscess treatment (Campos et al. 2021).

Human and clinical evidence

In the reported case, signs and symptoms of infection and inflammation resolved within five days after drainage followed by aPDT and PBM. At three months, no fistulous pathway or perianal collection was reported. Because all three treatments were combined, the case cannot estimate PBM’s added effect or recurrence risk across patients (Campos et al. 2021).

Animal evidence

In a rat anal-fistula experiment, daily low-level laser treatment reduced the area of the remaining tract, inflammatory infiltrate, and vascular congestion compared with no treatment. No animal had complete tract closure. This result concerns fistula tissue and does not test treatment of a perianal abscess in people (Dos Santos et al. 2021).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The abscess case combined PBM with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy and incision and drainage. The accessible report does not provide a complete, reproducible PBM dose set. The related rat fistula study used 660-nm red visible light at 4 J/cm², 3.57 W/cm², and 1.12 seconds per point. These animal parameters are not a tested protocol for abscess care (Campos et al. 2021; Dos Santos et al. 2021).

Interpretation

The case documents a favorable course after drainage and combined phototherapies, but it cannot show whether PBM hastened recovery or prevented fistula formation. The rat study found partial tract changes without complete closure and does not establish an abscess benefit in people.

Publications and records

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Very low for added benefit from PBM after perianal-abscess drainage

Only one combined-treatment case directly addresses abscess care (Campos et al. 2021).

Rationale for the certainty assessment

One case reported resolution after drainage, aPDT, and PBM, leaving PBM’s contribution untested. The related rat study addressed fistula, did not close any tract completely, and cannot establish abscess outcomes. No controlled human comparison estimates recurrence or fistula risk (Campos et al. 2021; Dos Santos et al. 2021).
